subject: DPA: roles, notify owners, and log preservation — follow-up
messages:
From: Kelli Zhang <kelli@healthsync.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@healthsync.ai>, HealthSync Legal <legal@healthsync.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Apr 2029 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from today — DPA clarifications and evidence ask

Hi Naomi —

Thanks for the demo and the candid discussion earlier today. A few things we want to confirm before we move to procurement:

- Controller vs Processor: we need a succinct statement of which party is controller/processor for the features we discussed (real-time text generation + embeddings). Can you confirm current position and what changes if we enable private deployment?

- Subprocessors: we'd like a current list (or a cadence for providing one) and the subprocessor notification window for any additions.

- Breach notification timing: we discussed an operational target on the call — please confirm the contractual notify window (we typically ask for <=72 hours for incidents impacting our data).

- Logs & retention: what logs are available (request logs, model input/metadata, system traces)? What's the default retention and do you offer configurable retention (we prefer 90 days for trial/proof-of-concept).

- Data residency: is there an option to keep all customer data (and backups) in a single US region (preferred: us-east-1) for the pilot?

I've attached a short spreadsheet with the items we want to track during procurement. If you can reply with a short answers + any evidence (SOC2, encryption docs, subprocessor list) that would help speed things up.

Appreciate it —
Kelli
Enterprise Programs | HealthSync
attachment: DPA_questions_healthsync.xlsx (spreadsheet, 24 KB)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.inference.com>
To: Kelli Zhang <kelli@healthsync.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Apr 2029 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — DPA clarifications and evidence ask

Thanks Kelli — great to meet you and the HealthSync team. Below is a concise recap and proposed next steps so procurement has what it needs. I'll loop legal and CS for attachments/evidence.

Short answers (high level):
- Controller/Processor: Redwood acts as processor for the inference API when you send data for model calls. If you require a private deployment (customer-managed VPC/on-prem), the roles are unchanged in the DPA language but operational controls (networking, KMS) move under your tenancy; we can include an addendum to clarify operational responsibilities for that mode.

- Subprocessors: We publish a current subprocessor roster; additions are communicated via email with a 30-day notification window by default. For enterprise contracts we can negotiate an extended notification or review window.

- Breach notification: Standard contractual target is 72 hours for incidents affecting confidentiality/integrity of customer data. We escalate earlier for high-severity incidents.

- Logs & retention: Default debug/trace logs retained 30 days; request-level audit logs retained 90 days for production customers on Dedicated or Private. Hosted free-tier may have shorter retention. We can configure 90 days for the pilot environment (including request metadata but excluding full model KV-cache contents).

- Data residency: We support pinning to a single region for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted, we can route to us-east-1 for your pilot and ensure backups/replicas stay in-region per the residency addendum.

Next steps / deliverables (proposed timeline):
1) Legal evidence pack (Marissa): SOC2 redacted report, encryption at rest/in-transit summary, KMS integration notes — target: 3 business days.
2) Subprocessor roster (Ben): current list + anticipated additions cadence — target: 2 business days.
3) Residency confirmation (Infra): confirmation that pilot can be pinned to us-east-1 and backup policy — target: 2 business days.

Marissa & Ben — can you confirm the attachments and confirm the timeline above? Kelli — if 72-hour notify, 90-day retention, and receipt of SOC2 + subprocessor roster are acceptable, we can draft the procurement-side statement and a short DPA addendum for private deployment.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
BizDev | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2029 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — DPA clarifications and evidence ask

On Mon, Apr 1, 2029 at 5:03 PM Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.inference.com> wrote:
> Marissa & Ben — can you confirm the attachments and confirm the timeline above?

Thanks Naomi — I can provide the legal evidence pack. Quick legal notes and what I'll attach:

- Positioning: Redwood's standard DPA states Redwood as processor. For Private deployments we include a paragraph clarifying operation-level responsibilities (key management, network control). I'll prepare suggested language for the addendum.

- Subprocessor list: we'll provide the current roster (GCP, Datadog, Logstore vendor, S3 backups) and a subprocessor addendum that offers a 30-day notice by default. If HealthSync requires a longer review period, we can flag that as a negotiable item.

- Evidence: I'll attach a redacted SOC2 report (SOC2-redacted.pdf), an encryption/crypto summary, and a short checklist of the items we can provide (certificate snapshots, KMS provider docs).

- Logs & retention: confirm that the team is aligned with providing a configurable 90-day retention for the pilot. Note: we do not retain unredacted model-token streams longer than the configured retention; model KV-cache is ephemeral and excluded from audit exports.

Attachments I'll drop in the shared Drive and attach here: privacy-evidence-checklist.md (checklist of docs we can share), SOC2-redacted.pdf.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy | Redwood Inference

From: Kelli Zhang <kelli@healthsync.ai>

Date: Wed, 3 Apr 2029 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — DPA clarifications and evidence ask

Thanks Naomi & Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- 72-hour breach notify is acceptable; please ensure the DPA reflects "notice no later than 72 hours after Redwood becomes aware" with operational escalation steps for critical incidents.

- 90-day configurable retention for request-level audit logs is acceptable for the pilot. We need the retention configurable via the Console or an API setting and a simple confirmation that exports (CSV/JSON) of audit logs will be available on request.

- Subprocessor roster: we prefer a monthly automated export of the active roster (just a small CSV). If you can provide a snapshot and an expected cadence for changes, that will satisfy our security review.

- Residency: us-east-1 for everything (primary data + backups) is a requirement for the pilot. Please confirm this can be guaranteed or state any exceptions.

- Evidence: SOC2 redacted + checklist + KMS provider name is sufficient for initial procurement. If possible, please provide the list of accessible encryption algorithms and whether customer-managed keys are supported in the pilot.

If you can confirm the above and share the evidence links (Drive + DocuSign stub) we can move to an SOW draft.

Kelli
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.inference.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — DPA clarifications and evidence ask

Kelli — all confirmed. Short deliverable list and owners: 

- SOC2 redacted + encryption summary + KMS notes (Marissa) — Drive link by EOD Wednesday (we'll drop the DocuSign stub for the DPA addendum there).
- Subprocessor roster snapshot + monthly export plan (Ben) — CSV and cadence doc by end of day Thursday.
- Residency confirmation for pilot in us-east-1 (Infra lead) — confirming via internal ticket; I'll update you no later than Thursday morning.
- Console/API retention control and log export instructions (Ben) — short how-to and API examples for 90-day retention export by Thursday EOD.

If that timeline works, I'll prepare a short procurement note (one-pager) that includes the DPA callouts and proposed addendum language for Private deployment. Once you confirm we will kick off the SOW draft.

Thanks again — looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
BizDev | Redwood Inference
